newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakhstan foreign investment hits $3.5 bln - govt.
newsitem.headline: Kazakhstan foreign investment hits $3.5 bln - govt.

text.p: Direct foreign investment in Kazakhstan has reached $3.5 billion, putting the Central Asian state second in the post-communist world in attacting foreign capital, a government official said on Wednesday.

"Kazakhstan is in second place, following Hungary, according to direct foreign investment per capita," government spokesman Amirzhan Khasanov told a news briefing, referring to countries in Eastern Europe and the former Soviet Union.
Khasanov did not provide a specific figure for per capita investment in Kazakhstan, which has a population of 16.9 million, but noted foreigners put in a total of $1.2 billion in 1996.
He said non-ferrous metals, oil-extracting and oil-processing were the main targets luring foreign investors.
Officials have previously estimated total foreign investment commitments to the resource-rich country at $40 billion.
Macroeconomic stability achieved last year was another strong signal for investors, Khasanov said.
The 1996 budget deficit was only two percent of gross domestic product, and inflation dropped to 28.7 percent from 60.3 percent last year.
